note: Default freshness profiles (Revalidating, V-1 to V-3): how long a record stays fresh, by record type, after Next.js cacheLife profiles. A venture overrides any of them under freshness in its naive.config.json, as a Next.js app defines cacheLife profiles in next.config.js. stale: how long an agent may reuse what it read without reading it again. revalidate: after this the record is stale, still readable with a stale flag, and should be checked or redone. expire: after this it is expired and not frozen into a release. per_phase: the record is stale once the venture changes phase after it was last checked. live: a fast-changing record, never frozen into a release; it stays a live hole. Durations are seconds, or a number with s, m, h, d or w. Version 0.x: ours and unevaluated.

live.note: Pipeline, money and streams: read from their system of record every time, synced at least weekly, never frozen

feedback.note: What customers said: stale after 30 days, too old to rely on after 90

research.note: Market research, product cards and site measurements: stale after 90 days

assumption.note: What the venture believes about its problem, solution, price and market: tested again each phase, and stale after 90 days

foundation.note: The strategic foundation: tested again each phase; in Discovery even confirmed statements are

max.note: Governance and other slow records: looked at again once a year

none.note: Generated or configuration records: never stale by time, only when what they depend on changes
